docs.text: A good grid is a grid you can read at a glance. JElib renders thumbnails for your assets — models, materials, HDRIs, and textures — and caches them for fast scrolling.

docs.title: Generate a thumbnail
docs.text:
Right-click one or more assets in the grid → Generate Thumbnail (or Generate N Thumbnails for a multi-selection). It works for models, materials, saved node trees, HDRIs, textures, and atlases.

A progress dialog shows while it renders. Geometry, HDRI, and texture previews run in the background so the panel stays responsive; material previews render in your live Houdini session.

Generate vs cache

Generate Thumbnail renders a new image. The Cache Thumbnails button in Preferences is different — it only pre-scales images you already have for faster display. See The thumbnail cache below.

docs.title: What each thumbnail shows
docs.text:
Asset How it's rendered Model An OpenGL shot of the actual mesh — no shaderball. Material / saved shader The material on a shaderball, lit with studio lights, in your active renderer (default Karma). HDRI The environment map itself, tonemapped. Texture / atlas A 2D preview of the image.

The renderer used for material previews follows the toolbar renderer selector.

docs.title: Auto-generate on save
docs.text: With Auto-generate on Save on (Preferences → Caching, on by default), JElib renders a thumbnail automatically whenever you save a 3D asset into the browser via Save to the browser. It skips assets that already have one, so it never re-renders needlessly. Right-click → Generate Thumbnail always works regardless of this setting.

docs.title: Style the material preview
docs.text:
Preferences → Thumbnail Appearance shapes how material previews look (models, HDRIs, and textures ignore these):

  • Use Simple Sphere — render on a plain sphere instead of the shaderball. Better for tiling materials, where the shaderball's grooves distract.
  • Use HDRI + HDRI Path — light the preview with an environment map instead of the default studio lights. Leave the path empty for the built-in default.

Caption Alignment sets where the asset name sits under the tile — Center, Left, or Right.

docs.title: The thumbnail cache
docs.text:
Thumbnails are stored as JPGs under your cache folder (Preferences → Caching → Thumbnail Cache, $JE_ASSET_BROWSER_CACHE). Two buttons manage the cache:

  • Cache Thumbnails — pre-scale every existing preview into the cache for fast grid display. This does not render new thumbnails.
  • Clear Cache — delete pre-scaled thumbnails and every generated geometry, material, HDRI, and texture preview. Original asset and vendor preview files are kept.

JElib also caches quietly in the background as you browse, so the grid fills in on its own.

docs.title: Manage a thumbnail
docs.text:
Right-click an asset:

  • Set Thumbnail… — pick your own image file to use as the asset's thumbnail, replacing the rendered one.
  • Open Thumbnail Folder — reveal the cached image in Explorer/Finder.
  • Delete Thumbnail — remove it; the tile falls back to a placeholder until you regenerate.

docs.title: Collect Files
docs.text:
Collect Files gathers every external file your scene depends on — textures, HDRIs, caches, USD references — copies them into one folder together with a self-contained copy of your hip file, ready for handoff, archive, or another machine. Your working scene is never modified: you keep working in your original file, and the portable copy sits in the target folder.

Where Relink Files rewrites paths in place, Collect physically copies the files and saves a portable scene alongside them.

Open it from JElib → Collect Files… in Houdini's main menu.

docs.title: 1. Choose a target folder
docs.text: At the top, Target is where everything gets copied — it defaults to $HIP/collects. Type a path or click Browse…. Editing it (or clicking Rescan) re-scans the scene.

docs.title: 2. Review what will be collected
docs.text:
Dependencies are grouped into a tree by where they'll land, with four columns:

Column Shows Destination the sub-folder each file goes to (with a checkbox — see below) Category its type (textures, geo, a whole vendor asset…) Size file/asset size Status ok, missing, cloud (online-only), or in_target (already there)

Include or exclude with the checkbox on each row — only ok files can be collected. Untick a folder to drop everything under it. For a loose image, a small dropdown lets you reclassify it between tex and render if it landed in the wrong bucket.

The running total above the buttons shows files · assets · size so you know how big the collect will be before you start.

docs.title: 3. Collect
docs.text:
• Collect copies the ticked files into <target>/<hipname>/ and saves a self-contained <hipname>.hip inside it — everything referenced $HIP-relative, so the folder works wherever you move it.
  • Collect & Zip does the same, then packs everything into a single shareable <hipname>.zip — the loose working folder is removed, only the zip remains.

You'll get a confirmation first (Collect N files … into {target}?), and a progress dialog you can cancel mid-collect — cancelling cleans up the partial copy and leaves your scene untouched.

Either way your session stays on your original file. A plain Collect ends with Self-contained copy saved — click Open collected hip to jump into the portable copy, or Close to stay put (the collected folder is revealed in your file manager). Collect & Zip reveals the finished zip instead.

docs.title: What it collects
docs.text:
Collect follows the same references as Relink — file parameters and any string parm pointing at a known media/geo file — and is smart about grouping:

  • Whole vendor assets. A file inside a Greyscalegorilla / Quixel / Fab asset brings the entire asset folder along, structure intact — not just the one map. PBR sets and model+texture bundles are copied whole too.
  • Sequences & UDIMs. $F frame sequences and <UDIM> tiles are gathered as a complete set, with the token preserved in the repathed value.
  • Name collisions are handled automatically — a colliding file gets a _1, _2… suffix so nothing overwrites.

Like Relink, it skips render outputs (ROP/TOP nodes), temp files, and expression-driven paths.

docs.title: Relink Files
docs.text:
Relink Files finds every external file reference in your scene, flags the ones whose files are missing, and lets you repoint them at files that already exist on disk. It's a pure in-place repath — it only rewrites the parameter's path; it never copies or moves files. (To gather the files themselves, use Collect Files.)

Open it from JElib → Relink Files… in Houdini's main menu.

docs.title: The window
docs.text:
The dialog scans your scene the moment it opens and lists references in a table:

Column Shows Node the node holding the reference (double-click to jump to it) Parameter the parameter name Path the file path (double-click to edit inline) Status Missing, OK, or → Pending (a staged change)

Missing references sort to the top. Missing only (on by default) hides the healthy ones; the Filter… field narrows the list live.

docs.title: Fix broken paths
docs.text:
Nothing is written until you Commit — every action below just stages a proposal, turning the row → Pending. That's your safety net: stage freely, review, then commit (it's a single undo, too).

  • Relink by Folder… — the fast path. Pick a New Root Folder and JElib searches it (recursively, case-insensitive) for files matching the missing names and stages the matches. Two fallbacks kick in for names that don't match exactly:
    • Other resolutions — if a texture no longer exists at its referenced resolution (a re-downloaded pack now shipping _4K_ where the scene expects _8K_), a popup lists the resolutions that do exist, largest first with counts. One pick stages every reference available at that resolution; the rest stay Missing, so re-run for stragglers.
    • GSG catalog renames — GSG files that were renamed across catalog re-releases (GSG_Terrazzo_34A_basecolor → GSG_MC010_A067_Terrazzo34A_4k_basecolor) are recovered by fuzzy matching: the texture channel must match exactly and only a clearly-best candidate is proposed (ambiguous cases stay Missing). These stage as → Pending (fuzzy 79%) — review the proposed paths before you Commit.
  • Find → replace + Apply — string-swap part of every path, e.g. $OLD_ROOT → $JOB. Works on selected rows, or all of them if none are selected.
  • Right-click a row → Browse for File… — pick a replacement by hand.
  • Use Relative Path / right-click Relativize Path — convert absolute paths to $ENV-relative where possible, for portability.

When you're happy, click Commit to write all staged paths at once. The status line reports what happened, e.g. Committed 12 path(s). (0 missing / 47 total). Closing the window with staged-but-uncommitted paths asks first — Commit and Close, Discard and Close, or Cancel — so staged work is never dropped silently.

Export a missing list

Export Missing… writes a text list of every unresolved reference — handy for chasing down files or handing the list to whoever has them.

docs.title: What it scans
docs.text:
Relink looks at Houdini's own file references plus any string parameter pointing at a known media or geo file (.exr, .tx, .abc, .usd, .fbx, and so on). It's token-aware — $F frame sequences and <UDIM> tiles are matched as a set, and a committed relink keeps the token in the parameter rather than pinning it to one file. Expression-driven paths (backtick chs(...) references and the like) are evaluated in context, so they show their real status — and relinking one preserves the expression.

It deliberately skips render outputs (ROP/TOP driver nodes) and Houdini temp files — those aren't broken input references.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: Quick fixes for the snags you're most likely to hit.

docs.title: The Browse grid is empty
docs.text: JElib isn't pointed at any assets yet. Add a library — see Add your libraries.

docs.title: My asset imported but has no material / renders untextured
docs.text: The material's renderer isn't loaded. JElib skips the material and still loads the geometry when the chosen renderer's plugin is missing. Switch the toolbar renderer to one you have installed and re-import. See Renderers & materials.

docs.title: Dragging a file from Explorer/Finder does nothing
docs.text: External drops need all three: the panel open (and visible, not behind another tab), the drop over the network editor, and Handle External File Drops on (Preferences → Import → Advanced). They don't work in the viewport or on parameter fields. See Import into your scene.

docs.title: My atlas scattered as one big grid
docs.text: The Atlas Splitter HDA isn't installed, so the atlas loaded onto a flat grid with no piece splitting. Install the HDA to trace the packed cards. See Texture atlases.

docs.title: An asset shows a ⚠ and won't load
docs.text: It lives on a remote/NAS source that's currently unreachable. Reconnect (check the NAS / Tailscale connection) and try again. See Remote & cloud libraries.

docs.title: New files I added to the NAS or a cloud folder aren't showing
docs.text:
NAS-synced libraries don't auto-detect new or removed files — a plain Reload click won't pick them up either. Shift- or Ctrl-click Reload to force a full re-walk of everything, or right-click the specific library in the tree → Reload This Library to force just that one.

Cloud-sync libraries (Dropbox/Drive/OneDrive/iCloud/Synology Drive) auto-detect changes on every reload by default — if new files aren't showing, check whether Preferences → Caching → Trust Cloud Library Cache Without Verifying is turned on. If so, that library behaves like the NAS case above and needs the same Shift/Ctrl-click or per-library force-reload.

docs.title: Thumbnails aren't appearing
docs.text: Cache Thumbnails only pre-scales previews that already exist — it doesn't render new ones. To generate missing thumbnails, right-click assets → Generate Thumbnail. See Make thumbnails.

docs.title: A scene's file paths are broken
docs.text: Use Relink Files to repoint references at where the files actually are.

docs.title: Updating
docs.text:
Inside Houdini: JElib → Check for Updates… When a newer release exists:

  • Free edition — choose Download & Install. JElib downloads the new version to your Downloads folder and updates itself in place. If that button isn't offered, use Open Download Page like the Paid edition.
  • Paid edition — choose Open Download Page, download the zip from your Gumroad library, then choose Install Downloaded Zip… and pick it.

A confirmation shows what will change, then JElib asks you to restart Houdini. Your libraries, favorites, and cache are all kept. Install Downloaded Zip… also installs an older zip if you ever need to roll back.

docs.title: Running the installer instead
docs.text:
Unzip the new version and run Install_JElib_Windows.bat / Install_JElib_macOS.command (or "<Houdini>/bin/hython" setup_jelib.py) exactly like a first install.

It detects your existing install and asks a single "Upgrade vX → vY in place?" On Yes it updates the code where it already lives and refreshes the package config without re-asking where anything goes.

Manual update

Unzip the new version over your existing JElib/ folder (keep user_libraries.json, favorites.json, and cache/), then restart Houdini — no package-config change needed if the folder path is unchanged.
